Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 amended Article 113(c): those Chapter III sections apply from 2 December 2027 for systems classified as high-risk under Article 6(2)/Annex III and 2 August 2028 for systems classified under Article 6(1)/Annex I. The preserved occurrence date/window (2022-07-20 through 2023-11-14) is before the earliest application date. Article 14(4)(e) therefore does not apply to this historical occurrence; this temporal disposition does not determine later system compliance or other legal duties. The taxonomy mapping generated a candidate only and does not make the requirement retroactive.

conclusion_change.previous: The evidence supports a provisional two-part governance interpretation. First, the complaint describes a population-derived prediction being treated as practically determinative of an individual patient’s post-acute coverage despite contrary clinical information; if established, that is an evidence-to-authority conversion rather than ordinary decision support. Second, the surviving contract claims and later discovery orders identify a distinct route question: whether a process represented as requiring clinical staff and physician decision-making was allegedly displaced by nH Predict. Both mechanisms remain allegation-bounded because the court has not determined that nH Predict actually dictated the named plaintiffs’ coverage decisions. The record therefore preserves the mappings at medium confidence rather than treating the litigation posture as proof of liability or of every pleaded factual claim. Both retained failure roles remain provisional on the explicitly pleaded mechanisms, without treating surviving claims or discovery orders as merits proof. The coverage-contract representation is a separate source-grounded process duty but has no matching admitted canonical EXTREQ; it is not relabelled as a later standards duty. The assessed EU, treaty and OECD versions are temporally excluded, and SDOS does not govern this predictive clinical/insurance workflow. No external requirement finding or medical-causation conclusion follows.
